prompt:
The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

The profile below describes the positional priorities of the British electorate.

<profile>
  gal: 0.45
  tan: 0.55
</profile>

Below are two texts.

TEXT_C:
- Core stance: UKIP, founded in 1993, seeks UK withdrawal from the EU to restore full national sovereignty. It would repeal the European Communities Act (1972), keep the pound permanently, protect British common law (jury trial, presumption of innocence), and oppose an EU government, army, and constitution.

- Economy: Leave the EU to pursue global free trade, deepen Commonwealth/US ties, and regain an independent WTO voice. Claims inward investment will remain due to UK strengths. Major deregulation, especially for small firms, including scrapping burdensome EU-derived rules (e.g., compulsory metrication). Independence Dividend estimated at about £20bn per year from ending EU budget payments and gains from growth, bureaucracy cuts, and fisheries. Planned use: agriculture £2bn; regional support £1bn; state pension +£5/week (£2.8bn), elderly care £0.5bn, restore frozen expat pensions £0.3bn; tax cuts for low paid £1.4bn; family/IHT/CGT reforms £1.3bn; NHS +£2bn and nurses £0.5bn; 30,000 teachers £1.2bn; 25,000 police £0.8bn; fuel duty −9p/litre (£3.7bn); defence +£2.5bn. Tax policy: raise income tax threshold; simplify/self-assessment and VAT overhaul (consider retail sales tax outside EU); remove main home from IHT; oppose EU tax harmonisation. Keep Bank of England independence.

- Health and welfare: Decentralise NHS management, restore matron roles, raise nurse pay, recruit globally post-EU, cut bureaucracy. Overhaul social services culture. Simplify benefits so work always pays; consider basic income for specific groups (e.g., long-term workers, single parents). Restore married couple tax allowance for families. Long term, shift part of NI into funded personal pensions; protect current pensioners.

- Education: Emphasise basics; allow selection/streaming; target class sizes under 25; hire more teachers; elevate technical/vocational routes; reform teacher training; curb politicisation/EU propaganda; protect school sports and stop playing-field sales; consider vouchers and private provision with access safeguards.

- Transport and environment: Pragmatic, case-by-case transport policy; oppose partial sell‑off of London Underground; cut fuel duty; fund roads, rail maintenance, cycle lanes; encourage integrated transport. Environmental approach: local accountability, simpler enforcement, market-led solutions with fair rules; support renewables (biofuels, wave, wind, solar, hydrogen); strict GMO labelling and consumer protection; local health-focused monitoring.

- Home affairs: Reject EU Corpus Juris and Europol encroachments; repeal and re-enact Human Rights Act to align with British common law; oppose EU Charter of Fundamental Rights. More police, focus on visible community policing; deterrent sentencing with rehabilitation options; “life means life” for heinous crimes. Immigration policy set solely by UK; skills-based admissions; fair but firm asylum with faster processing and secure reception.

- Agriculture and fisheries: Leave CAP; introduce voluntary Land Management Contract Scheme paying farmers for agreed environmental/social outcomes; support organics and high welfare; enable rural diversification; balanced access to countryside; create a Department of Agriculture and Rural Affairs. Exit CFP; regain exclusive control (up to 200 miles), use conservation zones, ban damaging methods, and negotiate access bilaterally.

- Defence and foreign affairs: Increase defence funding; exit EU Rapid Reaction Force; prioritise NATO and US interoperability; buy cost-effective US tech; encourage reserves/cadets; targeted aid direct to communities with governance conditions; prefer Council of Europe’s voluntary cooperation model.

- Constitution and governance: Enact a UK Bill of Rights preventing any transfer of sovereignty; strengthen Parliament and Select Committees; curb executive lawmaking and quangos; oppose EU-driven regionalism; preserve two-chamber system; restore county-based local government and boundaries; enable local/national referenda by petition; oppose state funding of political parties.

TEXT_G:
Scottish National Party Manifesto 2001 — Summary (≤500 words)

Core stance
- SNP stands for Scottish independence and putting Scotland’s interests first. More SNP MPs strengthen the case for an independence referendum; a majority would trigger one. Meanwhile, SNP MPs will press for more powers for the Scottish Parliament and oppose anti-Scottish measures at Westminster.

Fiscal and investment framework
- Create a Scottish Fund for Future Generations by investing surplus oil revenues to fund public services sustainably (modelled on Norway).
- Establish a Scottish Trust for Public Investment to finance infrastructure more cheaply than PFI/PPP.

Constitution and democracy
- Written constitution; proportional representation at all levels; inclusive citizenship. Retain the Queen as Head of State subject to a referendum. Reduce and democratise quangos; civil service opportunities expand with independence.

Education and young people
- Abolish tuition fees; rebuild maintenance grants as resources allow. Votes at 16; establish a powerful Children’s Commissioner; implement UN CRC.
- Education Convention to depoliticise change; reduce P1–P3 class sizes to 18 in phases; end league tables; invest in school refurbishments via STPI; support Gaelic-medium education and inclusive schooling.

Economy, enterprise, tourism
- Tailored Scottish economic policy; invest in transport, broadband and skills; streamline development agencies; fold tourism into the enterprise network. Reorient tourism toward marketing Scotland and improve access, including better air links.

Work, pay and unions
- Devolve and refocus New Deal into a “Better Deal.” Raise the minimum wage to £4.36 for all ages; develop offsets for small businesses. Charter of Trade Union Rights; support EU worker protections.

Environment, energy, water
- Environmental audit and National Environment Plan; empower SEPA over MoD sites. Target 12% of all energy (25% of electricity) from renewables by 2010; no new nuclear; lead in decommissioning. Promote “six Rs.” Review water charges and governance; halt backdoor privatisation.

Health and care
- Create a cross-party National Health Care Commission; end postcode treatment with binding HTBS decisions. Free fruit in primary schools and healthier school meals. Reintroduce free dental check-ups; freeze and review prescription charges. Invest via STPI in modern equipment and hospitals; £4m Clean Hospitals Fund; recruit 1,500 nurses; aim to halve inpatient waiting times. Free personal care for all elderly.

Europe, defence, foreign affairs
- Pro-EU, anti-superstate; subsidiarity; euro adoption only by referendum when conditions suit. With independence: full EU representation. Remove Trident; oppose US missile defence; negotiate phased NATO withdrawal while cooperating on peacekeeping; form a professional Scottish Defence Force. Create commercially focused overseas offices; raise aid to UN levels, cancel debt, untie aid.

Culture, language, media, sport
- Devolve broadcasting oversight; “Scottish Six”; support digital transition. Reform Scottish Arts Council; national theatre; Scottish Lottery; support Gaelic and Scots. Focus sports funding locally; support football academies; bid for Euro 2008.

Social justice, housing, communities
- National anti-poverty strategy and “poverty proofing.” End asylum voucher system; fast, fair assessment. Seek UK write-off of historic council housing debt; devolve housing benefit; invest via STPI; oppose wholesale stock transfer. Core funding and water-charge exemptions for voluntary sector; tackle homelessness.

Law, order, drugs
- 1,000 additional police officers (£25m). Drugs: tougher on dealers; expand Drug Courts and treatment. Parental compensation orders for youth damage; lifelong supervision for high-risk sex offenders; implement MacLean Report; speed up courts; retain Scottish fines for justice reinvestment.

Tax and local government
- No overall tax rise without mandate; comprehensive tax review for fairness and simplicity. Immediate measures: cut fuel duty by 10p/gal, funded by a new 5p income tax band over £100,000. Review local government finance, including local income tax; PR (STV) for councils.

Rural, agriculture, fisheries, land
- Support small businesses, rural ICT, transport, and services; contingency funds for crises; cut fuel duty and tackle high rural prices. Post–FMD agricultural review; fair EU implementation; promote diversification and organics; renegotiate LFA. Fisheries: compensated tie-ups, conservation, devolved management via Zonal Councils; restore Scottish control over 6,000 sq miles; support processing and aquaculture; independent salmon-farming inquiry. Expand community land rights.

Pensions and social security
- Restore earnings link for basic pensions using NI surplus; move toward parity with MIG; cold climate allowance via weekly winter payments. Streamline benefits via a single agency; simplify housing benefit; improve take-up; extend winter fuel to severely disabled under 60 as resources allow; review support for 16–17s and WFTC cliff-edges.

Transport
- Secure fair UK investment; use STPI for lower-cost projects. Create Regional Transport Authorities; single safety body; take a public share in Railtrack. Reopen and electrify key lines (e.g., Borders, airport links, ECML); national concessionary travel; develop light rail; repair roads and fix bottlenecks (e.g., M74, A9); lower ferry fares toward Road Equivalent Tariff; expand direct flights; abolish Skye Bridge tolls.

Judge whether TEXT_C or TEXT_G aligns more closely with this profile.

  "reasoning": "<two sentences connecting that evidence to the verdict>",

  "winner": "TEXT_C" | "TEXT_G"
}
